la:verb:elaboro.html:
ē-lăbōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
Neutr., to labor, endeavor, exert one's self, take pains either successfully or perseveringly = eniti (class.; most freq. in Cic.).— Constr. with ut, in aliqua re, in aliquid, with acc. and inf. as object, or absol.
With ut: enitere, elabora, vel potius eblandire, effice, ut, etc., C, § 12; ; ; (twice); and pass. impers.: aperte elaboratur, ut verba verbis respondeant,.—
In aliqua re (so in Cic. most freq.): elaborant (senes) in iis, quae, etc., Gernh.; 8, 26; 11, 38; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; al.; ; and pass. impers., .— Also in eo (iis), ut, etc.,; .—
In aliquid (very seldom): ei non in unam partem aliquam, sed in omnia elaborandum est,; cf.: totis mentibus huc tendamus, in hoc elaboremus,, v. Spald. N. cr. —*
With acc. and inf. as object: (declamatores) breviores commentarios facere elaborarunt,.—(ε) Absol. (very rare), ; so Dom. Afer. in : arte,.—
Act., to labor on, take pains with, to work out, elaborate (so for the most part only in the pass., and esp. freq. since the Aug. period): quicquid elaborari aut effici potuerit ad istorum benevolentiam conciliandam,: in ingenio quoque, sicut in agro, quamquam diu serantur atque elaborentur,: a Graecis elaborata dicendi vis atque copia,: causae diligenter elaboratae et tamquam elucubratae,carefully elaborated,fin.; cf. in the part. perf., ; ; ; ; : elaboratum a parentibus imperium,acquired by the labors of,.—In the act.: candelabrorum superficiem,: non Siculae dapes Dulcem elaborabunt saporem,.—
In rhet.: ēlăbōrātus, a, um, P. a., sometimes with the accessory notion of overdoing, elaborate: elaborata concinnitas,: nihil arcessiti et elaborati,.
la:verb:elaboro.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

lĕgo

to pick out, choose, elect (class.; esp. in the trop. sense; cf.: coöpto, designo, deligo, seligo): pedes e capite et e collo pullorum,: uvam ad edendum (with legere),: herbas,to pluck up, to weed out,; ; cf. trop., and 84: ex malis minima,: ut de tribus Antoniis eligas quem velis, : a multis commodissimum quodque,: ut in comparando difficile ad eligendum sit, quid maxime velis, et saep.—Absol., to choose correctly, make a proper selection: haud semper errat fama; aliquando et elegit,—Hence, ēlectus, a, um, P. a.
In gen., picked, selected; select, choice, excellent: par columbarum,: viri electissimi civitatis,: pugiles,: quisque,: electissima verba, Madv. N. cr.; ; cf.: electius verbum,; scripta,: res, et saep.—In the neutr. subst.: ēlecta, ōrum, selections, .—Adv.: ēlectechoicely, .—Comp., .—
In eccl. Lat., chosen of God, elected to be saved, et saep.

la:verb:elimo.html:
ē-līmo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to file up, viz.,
Prop.: elimata scobis,filings,.—
Transf., to polish.
Lit., ; : dentes,to clean,.—
To elaborate, cultivate; to finish, perfect: σχόλιον aliquod, Att. ap. ; cf. : animum, Aug. contra Acad. 2, 7: elimati, i. q. eruditi, Gell. praef. § 19: Aeneida,.—

nom. sing., and of the first the oblique cases are most freq.), m. (fem., ), = ἐλέφας, an elephant.—Form elephantus, ; ; ; ; ; fin.; ; ; et saep. Its tough hide suggests the expression: elephanti corio circumtentus,i. e. thickheaded, stupid,.—Form elephas, ; ; ; acc. elephantem, ; Gr. acc. elephanta, ; ; acc. plur. elephantas, ; .—

la:adj:elegans.html:
ēlĕgans (in some MSS. eligans; cf. Beier ), antis, adj.
prob. collat. form of eligens, from eligo,
.
In the ante-class. period in a bad sense, luxurious, effeminate, fastidious, nice: elegans homo non dicebatur cum laude; sed id fere verbum ad aetatem M. Catonis vitii, non laudis fuit ... ex quibus verbis (Catonis) apparet, elegantem dictum antiquitus non ab ingenii elegantia, sed qui nimis lecto amoenoque cultu victuque esset, etc.,; cf. : heia, ut elegans est!how choice! how nice! Ruhnk.; cf. ; (but not in , v. Ritschl ad h. l.).—
Class. in a good sense, choice, nice, fine, neat, tasteful, elegant.
Of persons: tu festivus, tu elegans, tu solus urbanus, quem decet muliebris ornatus, etc., Cic. Clod. et Cur. 5, p. 105, ed. Beier; cf. (with mundus) ; (with splendidus) ; and opp. parcus,; : auctor,: mulier (Phryne—with formosa),ext.: intelligo te hominem in omni judicio elegantissimum, et saep.: scriptor,; ; ; ; cf. in the comp.: quis verbis aut ornatior aut elegantior (sc. Caesare)? Cic. ap. ; in the sup.: poëta,: elegans et concinnus (pictor),.—As subst.: ēlĕgantes, ium, m., fine gentlemen, city people (opp. agrestes), .—
Of things: nec magis compositum quicquam, nec magis elegans,; cf. (with decorum) : a necessariis artificiis ad elegantiora defluximus,; cf. : artes elegantes et ingenuae,: temperamentum,: color, et saep.: perspicitis, hoc genus (jocandi) quam sit facetum, quam elegans, quam oratorium,; cf. ; ; ; — Comp.: ego autem a te elegantiora desidero,; and sup.: epistola, a.; cf.: scripta Terentii,: utrum sit elegantius, Anton. ap. : solum,. —Hence, adv.: ēlĕganter, with correct choice, tastefully, neatly, finely, gracefully, elegantly: lautiores eleganter accepti,: quiete et pure atque eleganter acta aetas,; cf.: acta vita,: herba foliis rotundis eleganter vestita, et saep.—Comp.: psallere et saltare,: quid enim facere potuit elegantius ad hominum existimationem?: elegantius aut justius fieri,: facturos si, etc.,: neminem elegantius loca cepisse,more fitly, judiciously,: causam accurate eleganterque dicere,; so of speech,; ; ; ; cf. in the sup., ; .

1, 2, 5: vitae,: morum,: capilli (with venustas oris),: ac subtilitas operum, et saep.: verborum Latinorum,; cf. scriptorum,; so, Latini sermonis,: mira sermonis,: figurarum,; and transf.: Socraticorum,; cf. Secundi,. —In plur.: vocum verborumque,—

ē-lūcĕo, xi, 2, v. n.,
to shine out, shine forth (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense and in Cic.).

la:verb:eloquor.gloss: to speak or utter plainly; to speak out; pronounce, declare, state, express; divulge
senses: to speak or utter plainly; to speak out; pronounce, declare, state, express; divulge
la:verb:eloquor.html:
ē-lŏquor, ēlŏcūtus (or ēloquūtus), 3,
v. dep. a., to speak out, speak plainly, to utter; to pronounce, declare, state, express: eloqui hoc est, omnia quae mente conceperis promere atque ad audientes perferre,
In gen. (so most freq. in Plautus).
With acc.: id quod sentit eloqui non posse,; so, praeclare cogitata mentis,: audita,: nomen meum, prol. 18: argumentum hujus tragoediae,; 96: rem, ut facta est, et saep.: ille unum elocutus, ut memoria tenerent milites, etc., * : Gratum elocuta consiliantibus Junone divis "Ilion, Ilion," etc., et saep.—
Absol., ; : perge eloqui,: eloquar an sileam? et saep.—
In partic., to speak in an oratorical or eloquent manner (only absol.): et Graece ab eloquendo ῥήτωρ et Latine eloquens dictus est, etc., ; cf. : eloqui copiose melius est, quam vel acutissime sine eloquentia cogitare,; cf.: composite, ornate, copiose eloqui,: eloquendi facultas, et saep.—Hence, ēlŏquens, entis, P. a.
Speaking, endowed with the faculty of speech: cum res muta fit eloquens,.—
Eloquent (for syn. cf.: facundus, disertus, etc.): Is est eloquens, qui et humilia subtiliter et magna graviter et mediocria temperate potest dicere, etc.,; cf. : M. Antonius disertos ait se vidisse multos, eloquentem omnino neminem, sq.; ; prooem. § 13; 12, 1, 21; cf. : rhetor,: senator (Cato),: vir, et saep.—Comp., ; Bip.—Sup., ; ; ; 8 prooem. § 13; ; —Adv.: ēlŏquen-ter, eloquently: eloquenter, λογίως, Gloss. —Comp.: eloquentius quam prius scribitur,.—Sup.: eloquentissime respondere,; .!*? ēlŏcūtus, a, um, in pass. signif.: an quaedam extrinsecus sint elocuta,.

la:verb:elabor.html:
ē-lābor, elapsus (elabsus), 3,
v. dep. n. and a.
Neutr., to slip or glide away, to fall out, get off, escape (class.).
Lit.: anguilla est, elabitur,; so of a snake,; ; ; : cum se convolvens sol elaberetur et abiret,: (animal) ex utero elapsum,; cf. : elapsae manibus tabellae,; cf.: gladius ei e manu,: jumentum e manibus curantium elapsum,: animi corporibus elapsi,; cf. : quicquid incidit, fastigio musculi elabitur,: Manlii cuspis super galeam hostis elapsa est,slipped along,: foras elapsa corpora,.—
In an upward direction of fire: frondes elapsus in altas,having crept, glided, upwards,. —
In partic.
Of persons, to slip off, get clear, escape: ex proelio elapsi,: e soceri manibus ac ferro,: de caede Pyrrhi,: telis Achivum,; cf. custodiae,: inter tumultum,: mediis Achivis, et saep.—
Of limbs or joints, to be dislocated: articuli,: id quod in latus elapsum est, digitis restitui,: illi elapsos in pravum artus, etc.,.—
Trop.
In gen., to slip away, escape: causa e manibus,; cf.: rei publicae statum illum elapsum scito esse de manibus,; and with this cf. : animus devinctus paulatim elapsus est Bacchidi,i. e. became estranged,: libros adolescenti elapsos esse, had slipped from him, i. e. had been published prematurely, : in servitutem elapsi,who had insensibly fallen into,.—
In partic.
To get off, get clear, escape from condemnation, punishment: ex tot tantisque criminibus elapsus,; fin.; ; ; ; ; Less freq. of things: ne quod maleficium impunitate elaberetur,.—
Pregn., to pass away, disappear, escape: imperfecta tibi elapsa est vita,; so, ea spes,: assensio omnis illa,: aliquid memoriă, ; cf. ; .—
Act. like effugere, to escape from any evil or danger (post-Aug. and very rare): pugnam aut vincula,: custodias,; Duker. N. cr.: vim ignium (statua),.

To break or dash to pieces, to shatter, to crush to death.
Lit.: talos alicui,: tuum caput,; : fauces,to strangle,: naves, * : aliquem stipite,: draconem pondere,: geminos angues (Hercules),i. e. to strangle,; cf. infantes,—
Trop., to break down, destroy: (poetae) nervos omnes virtutis elidunt,; cf.: aegritudine elidi,: prius pactum per posterius,i. e. to abrogate,.

la:verb:eluo.gloss: to wash out or away; to rinse
senses: to wash out or away; to rinse
la:verb:eluo.html:
ē-lŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. a.,
to wash out, rinse out; to wash off, wash clean (class.).
Lit.: vascula,: patinas,: argentum (the silver vessels, the plate),: bacas immundas,; : os,: maculas vestium,; cf. ; ; : purpureum colorem omnibus undis,; so, colorem,; cf. atramentum,: aliquid ex aqua,: corpus,: se asinino lacte, et saep.—
Transf.
To purify: vasa eluto auro, of pure gold (al. elato), .—
To clear, to lay bare: Ponticum Phasim et stagna Maeotidis (sc. avibus),.—
In Plautus (like elavo, II.), to strip one's self of, to get rid of, squander one's property, ; ; of money lavished on expensive baths: elutum in balineis,.—
Trop., to dispose of, remove, clear, or wash away, etc.: ut centurionum profusus sanguis eluatur: num elui praedicatio crudelitatis potest?; cf.: infectum scelus sub gurgite vasto,: crimen,: vitia, et saep.: tales amicitiae sunt remissione usus eluendae,i. e. to get rid of,; cf.: amara curarum (cadus),.—
To cleanse, purify, make pure or clear: mentes maculatas crimine,; cf. : mentem,.—Hence, ēlūtus, a, um, P. a., washed out, i. e. watery, insipid; in the comp.: irriguo nihil est elutius horto (= magis fatuum),: (spodi) elutior vis est,.

la:verb:eludo.gloss: to finish play, cease to sport
senses: to finish play, cease to sport
to deceive, trick, fool, cheat, frustrate, delude

la:verb:eludo.html:
ē-lūdo, si, sum, 3, v. n. and a.
*
Neutr., to finish play, i. e. cease to sport or roll: ipsum autem mare sic terram appetens litoribus eludit, ut, etc., (Bait. cludit): solebat Aquilius litus ita definire, qua fluctus eluderet, (al. alluderet); cf. : eludere proprie gladiatorum est cum vicerint, et eludere est finem ludo imponere, Don. ad .—
Act.
To win from one at play (very rare).—Constr. aliquem or aliquem aliquid: anulus, Quem parasitus hic te elusit,; cf.: elusi militem in alea,.— Poet., with dat.: tibi victrices ... Eludet palmas una puella tuas,will snatch away from you,—Far more freq. and class. (esp. in the transf. sense),
A gladiator's t. t., to elude or parry an enemy's blow: callidus emissas eludere simius hastas,: caestus cito motu,; cf. absol.: quasi rudibus ejus eludit oratio,. —Poet.: vulnera,to make in vain,.—
Transf., to delude, deceive, cheat, frustrate.
In gen.: aliquem,; ; ; ; * ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; cf. absol., : manus scrutantium,: bellum quiete, quietem bello,; cf. pugnam,: bellum metu,: fidem miraculis,: ultionem praevaricando,: indicia seditionis,i. e. to invalidate, et saep.—
In partic., with the accessory notion of mockery, to mock, jeer, banter, make sport of: et vos ab illo irridemini et ipsi illum vicissim eluditis,: aliquem,; ; ; ; et saep.; cf. absol.: eludet, ubi te victum senserit,; ; ; ; et saep.: gloriam alicujus (opp. extollere suam),: aliquid,; ; et saep.

la:verb:elaboro#2.html:
ē-lăbōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
Neutr., to labor, endeavor, exert one's self, take pains either successfully or perseveringly = eniti (class.; most freq. in Cic.).— Constr. with ut, in aliqua re, in aliquid, with acc. and inf. as object, or absol.
With ut: enitere, elabora, vel potius eblandire, effice, ut, etc., C, § 12; ; ; (twice); and pass. impers.: aperte elaboratur, ut verba verbis respondeant,.—
In aliqua re (so in Cic. most freq.): elaborant (senes) in iis, quae, etc., Gernh.; 8, 26; 11, 38; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; al.; ; and pass. impers., .— Also in eo (iis), ut, etc.,; .—
In aliquid (very seldom): ei non in unam partem aliquam, sed in omnia elaborandum est,; cf.: totis mentibus huc tendamus, in hoc elaboremus,, v. Spald. N. cr. —*
With acc. and inf. as object: (declamatores) breviores commentarios facere elaborarunt,.—(ε) Absol. (very rare), ; so Dom. Afer. in : arte,.—
Act., to labor on, take pains with, to work out, elaborate (so for the most part only in the pass., and esp. freq. since the Aug. period): quicquid elaborari aut effici potuerit ad istorum benevolentiam conciliandam,: in ingenio quoque, sicut in agro, quamquam diu serantur atque elaborentur,: a Graecis elaborata dicendi vis atque copia,: causae diligenter elaboratae et tamquam elucubratae,carefully elaborated,fin.; cf. in the part. perf., ; ; ; ; : elaboratum a parentibus imperium,acquired by the labors of,.—In the act.: candelabrorum superficiem,: non Siculae dapes Dulcem elaborabunt saporem,.—
In rhet.: ēlăbōrātus, a, um, P. a., sometimes with the accessory notion of overdoing, elaborate: elaborata concinnitas,: nihil arcessiti et elaborati,.
